Frame.text: The bike's main structure. Carbon is light and stiff, which is why it's the norm at this level.

Weight.text: Lighter bikes climb more easily and feel livelier. Brands usually quote a mid-size frame.

Tyre clearance.text: The widest tyre that fits. More room means more comfort and grip.

Tyres.text: Wider tyres run at lower pressure, which feels smoother and grips better.

Wheels.text: Deeper rims are faster on flat roads and in wind. Shallower ones are lighter and calmer in crosswinds.

Brakes.text: Hydraulic disc brakes stop strongly and predictably, including in the wet.

Groupset.text: The gears and shifting. Electronic shifting changes gear at a button press and stays perfectly adjusted.

Cockpit.text: Handlebar and stem. Integrated ones are cleaner and more aerodynamic, but harder to adjust.

Sizes.text: Brands label sizes differently. Use the brand's size guide with your height and inseam.

Rider height (cm).text: The brand's suggested height range for each size. A starting point only.

Stack (mm).text: The height of the front end. Higher means a more upright, comfortable position.

Reach (mm).text: The distance from the saddle area to the handlebars. Longer is more stretched out.

Head angle (°).text: A steeper angle steers quicker. A slacker one feels calmer.

Seat angle (°).text: A steeper angle puts you further forward over the pedals.

Head tube (mm).text: A taller head tube raises the handlebars without spacers.

BB height (mm).text: How high the cranks sit above the ground.

BB drop (mm).text: How far the cranks sit below the wheel axles. More drop feels more stable.

Chainstay (mm).text: Shorter feels more agile. Longer feels steadier and leaves room for wider tyres.

Wheelbase (mm).text: The distance between the axles. Longer is steadier, shorter is more agile.

Trail (mm).text: Affects steering feel. More trail is steadier, less is quicker.

Fork rake (mm).text: The forward offset of the front axle. It works with the head angle to set the steering.

Front centre (mm).text: The distance from the cranks to the front axle.

Standover (mm).text: The top-tube height you stand over. It matters when mounting and dismounting.
